definitions.label: Subtitle appearance
definitions.description: How subtitles are drawn during playback.
definitions.notes: Renamed from the unprefixed legacy key "subtitle_appearance". Every other canonical key carries a domain prefix, and preserving accidental key names is an explicit non-goal of the design. The rename touches three URL paths in internal/api/router.go, the admin device-settings routes, and the key constant in every client, so it cannot land without them. Migration copies the account-level legacy fallback to every existing profile and leaves device overrides unchanged, rewriting the key on each row. Revision 6 changes the fallback background from shadow to a 75% opaque box, matching the previous intended web default and the current Apple fallback. Connected clients receive the complete effective default from the server; clients should adopt revision 6 so their local and sparse-object decoding fallbacks match it. Stored profile and device overrides remain authoritative. Revision 14 adds the optional textOpacity property (1-100, default 100) controlling the opacity of the subtitle text itself, independent of backgroundOpacity; a value stored without it resolves to fully opaque text, matching pre-14 rendering.

definitions.label: Skip intros
definitions.description: What Silo does when an intro starts: leave it alone, offer a Skip Intro button, or skip it and offer an undo.
definitions.notes: The replacement for playback.auto_skip_intro, which could only say "prompt" or "count down then skip" and had no way to turn the prompt off. The default is "ask", which is exactly what auto_skip_intro=false did, so an untouched profile behaves identically across the cutover. The schema has no segmented control, so this is a select; clients that have a segmented control should use it. See docs/design/2026-08-16-intro-skip-mode.md.

definitions.label: Auto-skip credits
definitions.description: Move through end credits automatically when a skip is available.

definitions.label: Auto-play next episode
definitions.description: Continue to the next episode automatically.

definitions.label: Next up prompt
definitions.description: How long before the end of an episode the next-up prompt appears.
definitions.notes: Android currently writes player.next_up_prompt_seconds. That alias is migrated to this key and removed from production writes.

definitions.label: Metadata language
definitions.description: Fallback language Silo prefers for titles, descriptions, and artwork.
definitions.notes: Migrates user_profiles.preferred_metadata_language; that column is NOT NULL DEFAULT '', and the empty string means unset, so migration writes a row only where it is non-empty. Deliberately carries no constrained_by. An earlier draft declared an allowlist on policy input profile_preferred_metadata_language, which is circular: internal/policy/input.go populates that field from this very column and vendor/scope.rego relays it unchanged as a preference. Policy narrows nothing here, and an allowlist bound to a scalar equal to the current value would either be a no-op or reject every change the user makes. From revision 3, the private-use tag x-silo-original means resolve the target from each media item's original_language. It remains a valid value of the existing language_tag schema, so this is additive rather than a response-field type change.

definitions.label: Show advisory age
definitions.description: Show a recommended minimum viewer age from an advisory service, such as Common Sense Media, on item detail.
definitions.notes: Profile scope because the reader is a household parent deciding what a child may watch, and they browse on their own profile. Default false: the advisory is extra chrome most viewers do not want, and only the profiles that ask for it should carry it. This setting only controls whether the badge is shown: turning it on or off never changes what a profile is allowed to watch. Restricting a profile by advisory age is a separate access field, the profile's max_advisory_age, which a household manager sets on the profile itself. Coverage is partial by nature: the provider that supplies the advisory is rate limited per day, so on a large library some titles carry one and others do not.

definitions.label: Media cards
definitions.description: Poster size used by media cards.
definitions.notes: Semantic presets roam between like devices without forcing identical pixel dimensions across platforms. A profile fallback can opt into one presentation everywhere; family and exact-device values remain more specific. Revision 24 retires the caption choice: people hid titles and could no longer tell what a card was, so every card shows its title and details. caption stays required and keeps all three members so older clients can still write it, current clients send title_metadata and ignore the stored member, a migration rewrote stored values to title_metadata, and clients no longer offer it.
